name: Disclosure
description: A control that shows and hides one section of content, such as extra help under a form field. Use <details> and <summary>; for a set of related sections, use an Accordion.
summary: Shows and hides one section of content

elements.name: Summary
elements.description: Always-visible label that opens and closes the content

elements.name: Icon
elements.description: Triangle or chevron that turns when open

elements.name: Content
elements.description: Hidden until opened; can hold any flow content

variants.caption: Small — help text under a form field

usageNotes: Native <details> and <summary> work with the keyboard and screen readers without any script. Don't put links or other controls inside the <summary>.
If you build it from a button instead, set aria-expanded on the button and show or hide the content it controls, as in the ARIA Authoring Practices Disclosure pattern.
Use one Disclosure for a single optional section. For several related sections, use an Accordion; to switch between views of the same space, use Tabs.
Write a summary that says what is inside, such as "Help with your reference number", not just "More".
Don't hide content that most people need to complete the task. Leave it visible instead.
